title: An Idea Becomes a Connected System — Moonlit Linocut

scenes.title: Ink and carve the idea
scenes.purpose: Print the idea block: ink is rolled onto the left block and the lit bulb is carved out of it in positive-negative.
visuals: Brayer-edge ink roll left to right across the 600x624 block, with a fixed gouge grain
The bulb is carved out as a growing paper circle, and the rays are gouged outward from the bulb
The filament line draws, and the base bars rise into place
The heading AN IDEA prints left to right in a wipe

beats.development: Ink rolls across the block with a ragged brayer edge, and AN IDEA prints in from 0.10 to 0.52s.
The bulb is carved out of the ink. The rays are gouged outward in symmetric pairs, the filament draws and the base rises.

scenes.title: Connect the system
scenes.purpose: Turn the idea into a network. Telegraph dashes preview each link, then carved lines follow and the nodes are stamped as each line arrives.
visuals: Thin dashed telegraph lines lead each edge by 0.26s
Thick carved edges grow from their origin in breadth-first order from the block
Hatched nodes stamp in, pressing from 1.2x down to 1x
Hatch arcs that follow the form are carved on the bulb's shadow limb

beats.development: The links spread from the bulb panel out to six nodes. Each node prints when its line reaches it.

scenes.title: Name the system
scenes.purpose: Print the conclusion, then hold the finished print.
visuals: The hatched underline is carved from 2.10 to 2.50s

beats.development: SYSTEM and the hatched underline print in reading order.
Hold on the finished print, with all copy fully legible.

findings: The primary focus moves left to right: the block, then the network, then the copy.
Copy is revealed only in reading order. Each line is fully legible once its wipe ends.
More than 8% of pixels change: the ink roll alone covers about 40% of the canvas.
The background paper, frame and fixed textures stay stationary.
justifiedHolds: 2.5-3.0s: settled reading hold on the complete print

notes: Source-frame refresh: this uses the reviewed moonlit monochrome option (cool paper with indigo-black ink) instead of the earlier warm cream.

Techniques taken from the source review: a single tonal ramp, hatching anchored to objects, telegraph dashes before a strike, and lines that grow from their origin. The source's subject, characters, lettering and accent hues were not copied.
No preview recipe was supplied in STYLE.json.
